business.text: Avenue Supermarts Limited (DMart) is a national supermarket chain focusing on value-retailing across multiple product categories. The company primarily operates on a cash and carry business model along with sales to subsidiaries. It operates brick-and-mortar stores alongside the DMart Ready e-commerce platform and sells general merchandise and apparel largely consisting of private or pseudo-private labels.

cites.quote: Avenue Supermarts Limited (DMart) is a national supermarket chain, with a focus on value-retailing. We offer a wide range of products with a focus on the Foods, Non-Foods (FMCG) and General Merchandise & Apparel product categories.
The Company operates on business model of primarily cash and carry along with sales to subsidiaries and credit risk from receivable perspective is not significant.
The group operates on business model of primarily cash and carry and credit risk from receivable perspective is not significant.
They are actually all private labels or pseudo private labels.
Notwithstanding the opportunities that are available in DMart Ready. We do that too. But it is not either / or. I keep saying brick-and-mortar and e-commerce is the way to go.

narrative.text: The annual report and recent concalls align on DMart's physical retail store growth, reaching 500 stores and 20.58 million square feet of retail area while maintaining a cash and carry business model. However, management concalls place greater emphasis on the distinct operation of the DMart Ready e-commerce business, which runs at an EBITDA loss despite sales growth. Concalls also emphasize cost pressures not detailed in high-level annual report summaries, such as rising real estate prices, warehousing rental inflation, and wage increases that reduce return on capital.

bull.text: DMart expanded its footprint to 500 stores with 20.58 million square feet of retail area, operating successfully across states like Punjab, Tamil Nadu, Rajasthan, Gujarat, and Andhra Pradesh.

cites.quote: Since launching our first store in 2002 in Mumbai, Maharashtra, we have grown to 500 stores with a retail business area of 20.58 million sq. ft. spread across Maharashtra (128), Gujarat (75), Telangana (48), Andhra Pradesh (47), Karnataka (50), Madhya Pradesh (29), Tamil Nadu (35), Rajasthan (28), Punjab (24), NCR (20), Chhattisgarh (8), Uttar Pradesh (3), Uttarakhand (1), Goa (1), Orissa (1), Haryana (1) and Daman (1).
the fact that a DMart now is equally successful in the Punjab, as well as Tamil Nadu, as well as Rajasthan, Gujarat or in AP, in fact, simplifies a lot of things from an operating standpoint.

bull.point: DMart expanded its footprint to 500 stores with 20.58 million square feet of retail area, operating successfully across states like Punjab, Tamil Nadu, Rajasthan, Gujarat, and Andhra Pradesh.

bull.text: The company achieved a turnover close to INR 67,000 crores in the prior year while delivering 21% sales growth in its DMart Ready e-commerce business.

cites.quote: We reported a turnover of close to INR67,000 crores in the year gone by.
Avenue E-Commerce grew sales by about 21% and the loss slightly widened to about 7%, the loss was at INR247 crores.
Now, we have delivered a 21% or 22% growth rate vis-a-vis last year, purely on the DMart Ready business.

bull.point: The company achieved a turnover close to INR 67,000 crores in the prior year while delivering 21% sales growth in its DMart Ready e-commerce business.

bull.text: Credit risk from receivables remains insignificant, and the company has no history of loan defaults or being named a wilful defaulter.

cites.quote: The Company operates on business model of primarily cash and carry along with sales to subsidiaries and credit risk from receivable perspective is not significant.
The Company has not defaulted in repayment of loans, or other borrowings or payment of interest thereon to any lender.
The Group have not been declared wilful defaulter by any bank, financial institution, government or government authority.

bull.point: Credit risk from receivables remains insignificant, and the company has no history of loan defaults or being named a wilful defaulter.

bull.text: The business passes vendor price drops directly to customers, generates volume surges during staple price deflation, and reduced employee attrition to 11.3%.

cites.quote: we basically just pass through whatever pricing that is given to us from our vendors. So, we basically just ensure that the same is passed on whether it is price decrease or deflation or inflation.
So, whenever there is a deflation, you get huge volume pickup in those categories.
DMart employee attrition actually has fallen from last year, which we have published, I think it's fallen by almost 2% to 3%, from 13.9% to 11.3%.

bull.point: The business passes vendor price drops directly to customers, generates volume surges during staple price deflation, and reduced employee attrition to 11.3%.

bear.text: The DMart Ready e-commerce operations run at an EBITDA loss of minus 2% to minus 3% with annual net losses of INR 247 crores, impacted by higher transportation costs for home deliveries.

transportation costs have increased because home delivery has significantly increased.
EBITDA margin is still minus 2% to minus 3%.

bear.point: The DMart Ready e-commerce operations run at an EBITDA loss of minus 2% to minus 3% with annual net losses of INR 247 crores, impacted by higher transportation costs for home deliveries.
